Even so, the combined effect of furan, more secondary amide content, much higher N/O atom count, and higher basic pKa makes Neighbor 3 a clear mutagenic analog.

Neighbor 5 is another negative neighbor that nevertheless shares several mutagenicity-associated features with the query. On the other hand, the neighbor carries sulfonic halide while the query does not, so the delta is -1 for that feature, and that difference favors the non-mutagenic side here. Maximum partial charge also increases from 0.2608 to 0.4331 (delta +0.1723), which in this pair is another non-mutagenic shift. Even so, the presence of nitro together with the higher minimum absolute partial charge, stronger basic pKa, and more heteroatoms means Neighbor 5 still points toward the mutagenic label overall.

Neighbor 6 is the weakest of the six by similarity, but it still lands on the mutagenic side. Nitrogen/oxygen atom count rises sharply from 3 to 11 (delta +8), and heteroatom count rises in parallel from 3 to 11 (delta +8); both of those large increases support the mutagenic side in this comparison. The query has more basic sites, going from 2 to 5 (delta +3), but here that higher count is treated as unfavorable to the non-mutagenic outcome. Neutral fraction is very high in both molecules, but it decreases slightly from 0.9993 to 0.9974 (delta -0.0019), and that small shift is associated with mutagenicity in this local case. Even with that opposing effect, the nitro presence and the much larger N/O and heteroatom counts make Neighbor 6 another mutagenicity-supporting comparison.

The non-mutagenic signals are present too, especially around secondary amide count, QED, some charge descriptors, and ionizable-site burden, but they do not outweigh the repeated nitro/furan context and the broader heteroatom/basicity pattern. Taken together, the neighborhood evidence favors option (B): is mutagenic.
